title: Immigration
question: Who should be allowed to come live and work in the United States, and how should the rules be enforced?
summary: The rules for coming to the country, and the argument over how those rules should work. This page will stay with the big picture and will not lead with contested claims about voting.
sourceNote: Further reading only. This outline does not take facts from these pages yet. When the full page is written, government or other primary sources will be cited first, and the Just Facts page will stay linked as further reading. The wording on this site will stay original. No statistics are included here.

paragraphs: This section will explain, in calm language, what immigration law is for: who may enter, who may stay, who may work, and what happens when people are here without permission. It will define the words it uses, because “immigrant,” “refugee,” and “unauthorized” are not the same thing.
No statistics will be added until they are checked against primary sources.

This section will name the disagreement over how many people should be allowed to come, what skills or family ties should matter, and how firmly the rules should be enforced. It will give each side its strongest case, not its loudest slogan.

sides.intro: Each column will hold one side’s strongest fair case, in plain language and at similar length. Neither case is written yet.

a.title: One side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for one view, using checked facts. It will not use insults, and it is not written yet.

b.title: The other side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for the other view, under the same rules. It is not written yet.

This section will look for aims that are easy to miss in a loud debate, such as wanting a process that is understandable, wanting workers and families to be treated as people, and wanting the law that exists to mean something.

items: The questions will ask what a country owes people who want to join it, what it owes the people already here, and how to tell a checked fact from a claim that is still contested.
